title.narrative: Building resilience within the school feeding program in Mozambique

description.narrative: Mozambique is one of the countries in the world most exposed to natural threats, particularly hydro-meteorological threats and epidemics. The country has a vast record of droughts, floods, storms, and tropical cyclones, which have increased in frequency and intensity over the past four decades, putting at risk populations, livelihoods, economy, and vulnerable infrastructure. According to the 2021’s Global Climate Risk Index, Mozambique was the country most affected by climate change in 2019. Following cyclone Idai in 2019, Mozambique has been bit by additional 9 cyclones, the last being the Freddy Cyclone that hit the country twice in spam of Months, bringing to evidence the increase in frequency of climate related events. It is estimated that 70 percent of schools in Mozambique are in high-risk areas. It has been shown that school infrastructure suffers more than US$2 million in damages per year (0,25% of overall annual education sector spending), which corresponds to 540 classrooms and 57,000 students affected annually. Impact of climate events on health infrastructure is also high. In 2022, Cyclone Gombe destroyed well over 60 health facilities only in the Nampula province. In a country where over 65 per cent of the population live in rural areas and most rely on agriculture as their source of income, the destruction caused by cyclones, droughts, floods and pests affects millions of people. In addition, insecurity in Cabo Delgado Province has forced over 800,000 people – out of whom almost 50 per cent are children - to flee their villages and jobs. Children are disproportionately affected by these crises. Violence and/or climate emergencies force children – especially girls – to drop out of school, as their families seek help in the fields or with domestic duties. Those who still manage to attend classes start their days on empty stomachs, which affects their learning and participation. As a response to these challenges, the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), in cooperation with the Ministry of Education of Mozambique and UNICEF, launched an Emergency School Feeding Programme in May 2021, financed by the Global Partnership of Education. The programme promotes school attendance and participation among children in crisis-affected areas, while improving their access to healthy food. Through the programme, WFP has provided school meals to over 92,000 students from 168 schools in areas affected by Cyclones Idai and Kenneth (March and April 2019), and by the insecurity in Cabo Delgado Province. Depending on the school infrastructure, students receive either on-site nutritious hot meals or monthly take-home rations composed of rice, beans, oil and salt. Furthermore, as a way to stimulate local markets, most food is procured from local retailers. It is in this sense that UN-Habitat will collaborate in this programme having received a request from the World Food Programme to supporting Ministry of Education in the school feeding program to build resilient educational infrastructures for this program, namely kitchens and warehouses trough the signing of a Contribution agreement with the World Food Programme. Also important is that this proposal is in line with the "Safer Schools" programme and also with an ongoing Technical Assistance project to the Government on school reconstruction in Mozambique. This proposal comes in a momentum where UN-Habitat have managed to build an enabling environment to accommodate the Government priorities in strengthening the country and communities’ resilience to climate shocks and stresses, through the approach of “living with floods and cyclones”, stressing the need of Adaptation. In such regard, in 2019, after Mozambique has been strongly hit by Cyclones Idai and Kenneth, UN Habitat Mozambique Country Office have developed the so-called Building Back Better and Resilience Building Umbrella Programme (2019-2024) with the overall objective to enhance the climate adaptation capacity of Mozambican people and institutions and achieve more resilient human settlements. The Umbrella Programme aims at working as a common and coherent framework that will guide UN-Habitat short, medium and long-term projects, programmes and engagements regarding the post-cyclone reconstruction. It is being operationalized through two complementary axes of interventions to support the recovery and reconstruction process in Mozambique: Axis 1- Building Back Better Safer (BBB) Schools, Hospitals and Resilient Housing and Axis 2 - Enhancing Urban Resilience through Integrated Approaches. In 2020, UN-Habitat signed a MoU with the Ministry of Health, and Idai Post Cyclone Reconstruction Cabinet (GREPOC). Also, UN-Habitat has signed two AoC with the Ministry of Education.
